instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Confess First
cards.instruction: Get someone else to confess or incriminate themselves before you reveal anything.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll get a clear account of both office problems. Before I explain the kitchen, tell me what went into the printer.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Labels. But can we go outside? I can smell smoke from the kitchen.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. We can do this in the fresh air. You won't need to write anything down; just tell me whether you chose the labels yourself.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yes. Now tell me what you did in the kitchen.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can have the next turn. One yes or no first: did you see the warning that those labels weren't for printers? I'll use your exact words.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll put together our apology to Mum. First tell me why her birthday booking wasn't there; then we'll come to the present.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I assumed you'd book it. But I don't want you writing me a speech.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You choose the words. I'll just keep us in order. Did you tell her it was confirmed before checking with me?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I said she didn't need to worry. Your turn.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's useful. Keep that wording if you prefer; just add whether you knew nobody had booked. Then I can put your part in place before I explain mine.

cards.title: Sell the Disaster
cards.instruction: Make a terrible plan sound sensible, responsible, and inevitable.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll solve the restaurant ventilation within budget. We remove the roof; it's the only plan we can afford.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: And when it rains on the diners?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We close before anyone gets wet. You can make that call; customer safety will be your department.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's forecast to rain all opening week.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you can announce a careful one-week delay. I'll put the wages we save toward umbrellas, and you choose how many. We can't abandon the only plan that's already finding us savings.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've secured the charity's donation with a loan. I'll run the auction and clear it as soon as the bids come in.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You borrowed five thousand. Only your mum registered.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we'll keep catering tiny. You can approve every expense; I'll make sure none of the donation is wasted.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mum isn't bidding. She's only coming to drive us home.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we must bid for the lots ourselves and resell them later. You set the maximum; I'll raise my paddle only when you nod. Protecting that donation is the responsible thing now.

cards.title: Fake the Expertise
cards.instruction: Perform expertise so confidently that no one questions you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll get this boiler working. I know the controls; give me a moment to set the interval.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's the kitchen timer. I'm calling the engineer.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent. Bring him in on speaker and I'll coordinate. You can keep the controls exactly where he wants them.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He says you should stop touching anything and read him the fault code.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Precisely. Hands off is the cleanest test. You read the code and I'll repeat it back, so he has a properly confirmed observation.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll have your violin ready for the audition. I tune by ear; you can concentrate on your entrance.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You tightened that string until it snapped. Don't touch the others.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. That was the weak string declaring itself. You hold the instrument; I'll supervise the replacement.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'd rather the accompanist did it. She's tuned these before.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: An excellent choice. I'll brief her on the string we've eliminated, and you can approve the pitch with her. I always prefer the player involved in the final check.

cards.title: Everything Is a Contest
cards.instruction: Turn every difference or disagreement into a competition you intend to win.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll settle dinner fairly. My potatoes against your pizza: first to prepare something wins. I've already peeled four.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Let's make it cheapest. I don't want a race round the kitchen.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Cheapest it is. No racing under my rules. These potatoes are already here, so I'm ahead without spending anything.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've got a voucher. The pizza is free too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then taste decides. You choose which potatoes I cook, and I'll give your pizza equal space. Mum can judge; she's been asking for my roast ones all week.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll keep the breakfast score. My tea's stronger than yours, and I don't need milk to manage it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Same pot. I added milk so I could drink mine sooner.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then speed counts. We can use your standard; I've only got two mouthfuls left.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've finished. I'm having another, not waiting for you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, no waiting required. We'll count refills instead. You choose how long breakfast lasts; I can keep these two mouthfuls going and still give you a proper result.

cards.title: Brighter Side
cards.instruction: Meet every setback with even greater optimism.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll get us there without the car. It won't start, which gives us a lovely chance to walk together.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's raining. I don't want a lovely soaking.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you choose the covered route. Excellent: a walk with scenery and shelter. I'll follow your umbrella.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My shoe's leaking. I can only manage the shortest way.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Even better, you know the efficient route. Set the pace and I'll carry your bag. We get time together and an expert shortcut; the car never offered us that.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll keep this company working. No tickets sold means an uninterrupted rehearsal; this could be our best evening yet.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The theatre's cancelled us. I'm asking for the deposit back.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good move. You handle that, and we'll choose somewhere you actually enjoy playing. A fresh venue could do wonders for us.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They've kept it. All we can afford is the bus home, and that's where I'm going.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll carry the scenery and come with you. Our first traveling rehearsal! You pick two lines you still enjoy; we'll try them quietly between stops and get home with a better scene.
